The workshop runs over **three days** at **Knight Campus Building 2**, University of Oregon — **Wednesday–Friday, June 10–12, 2026** — with an **optional Day 0** the day before (**Tuesday, June 9**). The day-by-day plan is below; every session's lecture, reading, tutorial, and Talapas script lives on the **[Materials](Materials.qmd)** page.

::: callout-tip
**Before Day 1:** complete the [Software Setup](Software_Setup.qmd) on the laptop you'll bring. Plan 30–60 minutes, the day before — *not* the morning of.
:::

## What to bring

- **Your own laptop** with at least **16 GB RAM** and **~10 GB free disk** — the workshop is hands-on and there are no lab machines
- R ≥ 4.4 and RStudio Desktop installed (see [Software Setup](Software_Setup.qmd))
- The workshop packages and dataset installed ahead of time (see [Software Setup](Software_Setup.qmd) and [Module 00](Materials.qmd))
- A power adapter — outlets are limited in the conference room

## Day 0 (optional) — Software Setup & Computational Refresher

Offered on **Tuesday, June 9** (same room) as **two identical sessions** — **10:00 am – 12:00 pm** and **3:00 – 5:00 pm**. **You only need to attend one;** come to whichever fits your schedule. Both sessions cover the same material, so **drop in for the parts you need** and bring your laptop along with any install problems you couldn't solve on your own.

Each session covers, as time and demand allow:

- Laptop setup help — R, RStudio, and the workshop dataset
- Installing R / Bioconductor packages in R & RStudio
- R fundamentals refresher — tidyverse, writing functions
- Unix command line — `cd`, `ls`, pipes, `grep`, `wget`

## Bonus tracks — self-paced after the workshop

The following modules are **not part of the three-day in-person workshop**. They ship alongside the workshop materials for you to work through on your own time once you've finished the core sequence:

- **Module 09** — Bulk and single-cell ATAC-seq with Signac
- **Module 10** — WGCNA on bulk RNA-seq
- **Module 11** — Spatial transcriptomics with Visium
- **Module 12** — Trajectory inference & cell–cell communication
- **Module 13** — FAIR principles and data submission
- **[Full Talapas RNA-seq run from raw FASTQs](Additional_Resources.qmd)** — the entire pipeline on UO's HPC starting from raw reads and Cell Ranger, on a real 10x dataset (in Additional Resources)

## During-workshop support

The instructors will be in the room throughout the workshop. For questions outside workshop hours, email is the most reliable channel — see the [About](about.qmd) page.
